title: Hacked Site Recovery
description: Respond to a compromised WordPress site — isolate, clean malware, close entry points, and restore from clean backup.

steps.title: Isolate the Site Immediately
steps.instructions: Put the site in maintenance mode or block public access. Change all admin, FTP, database, and hosting panel passwords before investigating.

steps.title: Document Hack Symptoms
steps.instructions: Note spam redirects, injected scripts, unknown admin users, pharma spam in search results, or hosting suspension notices. Screenshot evidence for records.

steps.title: Scan for Malware and Backdoors
steps.instructions: Run Wordfence, Sucuri, or MalCare scan. Check wp-content/uploads for .php files, suspicious mu-plugins, and modified core files. Compare checksums with clean WordPress.

steps.title: Remove Malicious Code and Files
steps.instructions: Delete unknown plugins, rogue admin users, and injected code in theme functions.php, wp-config.php, and .htaccess. Do not trust infected files — replace from clean source.

steps.title: Reinstall WordPress Core and Audit Themes
steps.instructions: Upload fresh wp-admin and wp-includes. Replace active theme with a clean copy or default theme. Remove nulled/pirated plugins — common infection vectors.

steps.title: Close the Entry Point
steps.instructions: Update all plugins and PHP. Revoke all Application Passwords. Fix weak credentials, outdated plugins, and file permission issues (no 777). Block xmlrpc.php if abused.

steps.title: Restore from Clean Backup if Needed
steps.instructions: If malware is widespread, restore files and database from a known-clean backup before the infection date. Re-apply legitimate changes made after that date manually.

steps.title: Harden Site and Monitor
steps.instructions: Enable 2FA, file change monitoring, and least-privilege user roles. Submit reconsideration request to Google if blacklisted. Monitor for 30 days post-recovery.
